entry.dc:title: Prospects of Development of the Krivoy Rog Iron Ore Basin.
entry.dc:creator: Nivalov N.N.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Krivoy Rog basin is the largest iron ore basin in the world. In 1974, its output of commercial ore amounted to 107 M t. Rich ore deposits are estimated at 1. 5 G t; with 57. 9% iron content, 1. 3 G t of them of industrial categories. In 1975, over 45 M t of commercial rich ores were mined. The resources of ferruginous quartzites down to the depth of 500 m are estimated at 14. 9 G t. Five ore-dressing combines produced 61. 6 M t of ore concentrates with 65. 04% iron content in 1975. Future prospects of the basin are described. It is proposed to divert the river Ingulets and to build a super open pit mine with the design depth of up to 1000 m and annual output capacity of 150-180 M t of raw ore.

entry.dc:title: Prospects of Development of the Iron Ore Base and Ensuring Supply of Iron Ore Raw Material for Metallurgical Plants of the urals Economic Region.
entry.dc:creator: Gorshkolepov M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Since 1960, the iron ore industry of the Urals has been forced to rely on increasing output of poor ore grades with unchanged output of commercial ore. There are 88 iron ore deposits in the Urals, amounting to 15% of the overall USSR resources. They are represented mainly by titanium-magnetite ores poor in iron. Large metallurgical plants in the Urals constitute 28% of the pig iron industry of the USSR. They consume 52-53 Mt of ore per annum while the output of commercial ore in the Urals and Kazakhstan amounts to 45 Mt, i. e. 86-88% of the required amount. Even by 1980 the deficit in local and Kazakhstan ore will amount to 5-6 Mt. The plans to increase the output of the Kachkanas open pit mine and to build another mine there with an annual output of 45 Mt of raw ore, as well as to develop smaller deposits by 1980, are outlined.

entry.dc:title: Effect of the Methods of Transportation of Large-Sized Open Pit Mine Equipment Assemblies on Time-Limits and Cost of Its Manufacture.
entry.dc:creator: Chernegov Y.
entry.dc:description: An analysis is presented of the constraints on the manufacture of large-sized equipment units imposed by the limitations of road, railroad and air transportation capabilities. It is suggested that a fleet of airships be built in the USSR to transport large-sized mining equipment components.

entry.dc:title: AMERICAN CONGRESS ON SURVEYING AND MAPPING, FALL CONVENTION, PROCEEDINGS, 1975.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc Am Congr Surv Mapp Fall Conv
entry.dc:description: Thirty-two papers, eight abstracts, and fourteen titles by various authors are presented. The topics discussed are: Terrestrial cameras, layout machines, electronic distance measuring, boundary disputes, cadastral standards, dendrology, computer mapping, reproduction techniques, aerial photography, trilateration, defense mapping, three dimensional deadload deflection, topographic information bank, surveying education, cognitive maps comparison methodology, cartographic raster scanners, ultra-precise control nets, open pit mine surveys, Doppler satellite point positioning, planned unit developments, satellite imagery, national mapping requirements, technical obsolescence, automated map compilation, cartographic data bases, slope maps, new Colorado maps, multi-dimensional analysis processing system, digital mapping, Skylab imagery, space photography, aerotriangulation, and Skylab cartography. Selected papers are indexed separately.

entry.dc:title: SACATON - ASARCO'S NEW COPPER MINE IN ARIZONA.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: American Smelting and Refining Company (Asarco) has put into operation its newest major producing copper mine, the Sacaton unit, near Case Grande in Arizona. The open pit mine and concentrator was developed by Asarco at a cost of some 40 million. Currently the mine is building up to its full planned production rate of 21,000 ton/year copper in concentrates from a mill throughput of some 9,000 ton/day. The new mine area encompasses two separate orebodies. The shallower orebody is the one now being mined, and it is planned to phase in underground operations at a later date in the deeper lying orebody. The shallow west orebody varies in thickness up to 700 ft and contains about 33. 9 million tons of porphyry-type ore averaging 0. 76% copper taking a 0. 3% cut off grade. The smaller and deeper east deposit is about 300 ft thick and contains about 14 million tons of ore grading 1. 37% copper.

entry.dc:title: EXPANSION PROGRAMME AT PALABORA.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: This article descrives a major expansion program undertaken by the Palabora mine, South Africa's most important copper producer, which will increase refined copper output to 125,000 metric tons/yr. The program is designed to enable Palabora to retain its place as one of the world's cheapest copper producers. At the new mining rate, the open pit mine will have a life of about 20 years. Plans for an underground mine to replace pit production in the 1990's are also discussed.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINE SURVEYS.
entry.dc:creator: Noice G.V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc Am Congr Surv Mapp Fall Conv
entry.dc:description: Overview of methods used for modern open pit mine surveying in control, daily routines, slope stability, drill locations, computations, land surveying and construction is given. Control is established by resection, triangulation, or traverse based on a tight control network on the surface. A unique slope stability monitoring program is operated using an HP3805 and a Lietz TM1A. Data are shown in graphical form.

entry.dc:title: Justification of the Construction of a Mathematical Model of the State of Operations at an Open Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Cheremkhin Y.P.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A mathematical model of an open pit mine, relying on the method of vertical cross-sections, is developed. It permits one to obtain data on the state of the mining operations more easily, to arrange for automatic data transmission through the system until its complete destruction, to improve the precision of the determination of the volumetric indices of mining operations.

entry.dc:title: Experience of Designing a Skip Hoist for the Sibayskiy Open Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Simakov P.
entry.dc:description: In 1971, the West German firm ″Siemag″ delivered a strip hoist for the Libayskiy open pit mine in Kazakhstan. The design depth of the mine is 490 m. The first stage of the hoist trench, to the depth of 180 m, is 286 m long, 14. 5 m wide, has an inclination of 39 degree , and is provided with two rail tracks, each 3070 mm wide. The hoist is equipped with two 40-ton skips. Construction problems and solutions are briefly related.

entry.dc:title: PINTO VALLEY, NEWEST ARIZONA COPPER PORPHYRY; MINE 40,000 DAILY TONS ORE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Pinto Valley copper mining complex has completed its start-up phase, and is now in continuous operation with the ability to exceed design throughput of 40,000 tons of ore per day. One of the larger copper mines in Arizona, Pinto valley is expected to produce 62,500 tons of copper per year, plus some molybdenum. The ore body will provide a 24-year ore reserve, based on an initial production target of 40,000 tons per day ore and 60,000 tons per day of waste. The estimated 100,000,000 project, the largest single construction project ever undertaken by Cities Service Company, includes the Pinto Valley open pit mine, a 40,000 ton per day concentrator, and a 10-mile slurry pipeline that transports a 28 percent copper concentrate slurry to a new filter plant located in Miami.

entry.dc:title: BLACK SEA COPPER - GEOLOGY, DRILLING DATA, PIPELINE DESIGN.
entry.dc:creator: Ethem M.
entry.dc:description: The Black Sea Copper Works Corporation operates several open pit and underground copper mines, flotation mills, a 50-mile long concentrate pipeline, and a 40,000 annual metric ton blister copper flash smelter along Turkey's Black Sea coast. This article has been prepared with the intention of giving more detailed information on specificc aspects of the project such as: Geology of the Murgul area (Cakmakkaya and Damar open pit mines) and Kure area (Asikoy open pit mine and Bakibaba underground mine) and vertical development chart of the Bakibaba underground mine.

entry.dc:title: Open Pit Method of Mining Ferruginous Quartizites in the Krivoi Rog Basin.
entry.dc:creator: Statkevich A.A.
entry.dc:description: Between 1955 and 1968 five ore-dressing combines have been built in the Krivoi Rog basin. They treat ferruginous quartzites mined from 9 large open pit mines whose projected depth reaches 300-500 m and annual capacity from 5 to 36 million t of crude ore. The annual capacity of the combines is: 135 Mt of crude ore and 60 Mt of concentrate with the iron content of 64-65%. The article gives a brief description of all the combines of the open pit mining methods, transportation, waste disposal and recultivation of the stripped soil. Plans to deepen open pit mines to 450, 500 and even 800 m are outlined. A project of construction of a super-ore-dressing combine with the capacity of 150-180 Mt of crude ore per annum with an open pit mine 900-1000 m deep is mentioned.

entry.dc:title: Geology of the Biwabik Iron Formation, Dunka River area, Minnesota
entry.dc:creator: Bonnichsen B.
entry.dc:description: Applied geology at the Nickel Mountain nickel-silicate mine, the only producing nickel mine in the United States, in its broader aspects is little different from that where mining geology is used extensively in mining metallic mineral deposits. Important differences arise, however, because of the nature of the ore deposit, its general geology, mineralogy, structure, rock alteration, chemistry, and origin, all of which are unique in North America. The Riddle ore bodies are nickel-silicate or nickel-bearing saprolite deposits that probably represent the erosional remnants of original nickel-laterites that formed on old erosion surfaces by weathering and supergene enrichment. Much of the initial, deep, residual products of weathering now have been removed by erosion, leaving a complex blanket of decomposed, leached, and enriched saprolite that grades laterally and downward into fresh peridotite and dunite. The ore mineralization extends downward along a rather definite fracture and fault system forming nickel silicate-chalcedony (or boxwork) veins in depth. Applied geology consists of (1) the collection of geologic facts by open pit mine mapping, drilling and laboratory work, and (2) the use of geologic data in ore reserve computations, mine planning, grade control and study of special problems relating to mining, beneficiation, and smelter operation. Each of these pursuits has important and interesting ramifications owing to the characteristics of the ore deposits and the reliance that must be placedo n the geological work for successful mine operation. Grade control, which includes not only the control of nickel grade but also the selection of ores to be blended for optimum smelter performance, is perhaps the single most important aspect of applied geology and essential to the successful operation of the mine.

entry.dc:title: Container Pneumatic Transport at Mining Enterprises.
entry.dc:creator: Vasil'ev M.
entry.dc:description: Special characteristics and prospects of application of container pneumatic transport at open pit mines are considered. Several existing and planned systems of this kind in the USSR are described. It is concluded that pneumatic pipeline transportation with the use of containers can be advantageous in some cases in shallow open pit mines (up to 80 - 100 m deep) with the capacity of up to 10 million t p. a. to deliver a mineral to a separation factory situated at a distance of 3 - 5 km or more, with preliminary crushing at the open pit mine to a coarseness not exceeding 280 - 300 mm.

entry.dc:title: Procedure of Selecting and Changing Open Pit Stripping Schedules (Using Motor Transportation).
entry.dc:creator: Istomin V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Planning of open pit mine stripping schedules is carried out with consideration of their possible restructuring in accordance with the dynamics of the mining work. Laboriousness of the multi-variable selection of schedules is reduced, thanks to an aggregate determination of the indices of operation of the motor transport and the use of the dynamic programming method.

entry.dc:title: DEFINITION OF DESIGN JOINTS FOR TWO-DIMENSIONAL ROCK-SLOPE ANALYSES.
entry.dc:creator: Steffen O.K.H.
entry.dc:description: Analysis of the stability of rock slopes can be performed using a three-dimensional or a two-dimensional analysis. The relative importance of various factors incorporated in a two-dimensional analysis are examined and a method proposed for determining reliable average values for dip angle, dip direction and joint spacing of the joints belonging to a joint set. Observational errors in recording of dip direction and dip angles are analyzed for a joint survey carried out in an open pit mine. Results obtained from a two- and three-dimensional analysis are compared for an open pit mine slope.

entry.dc:title: DEVICE FOR CHARGING WET BLASTHOLES.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: A new Swedish invention known as the Wangu has been designed specifically for charging blastholes with Anfo and slurries. The primary purposes of the Wangu IIB unit is to protect Anfo against water in blastholes. Wangu consists of three main parts: the nose cap, the container and the thin plastic bag. The plastic bag, which can be as long as the borehole is deep, is folded and protected before use in the container. The nose cap protects the insulation of the electric wires and prevents water getting backwards in the container through the evacuation channels. These parts are intended to be used once and thereafter thrown away. The procedure for charging a borehole is exactly the same with or without Wangu. The loader is filled with explosives and charged with compressed air. From the carton of Wangu one of the correct dimensions is selected. The primer and perhaps a dynamite chargeis put in the nose cap and the Wangu attached to the filling hose. Charging can now take place normally. Results of testing the Wangu technique at the Boliden open pit mine are given.

entry.dc:title: Investigation of Prospective Contours of Open Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Sakantsev G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A method is proposed for the determination of promising outlines of open pit mines. It is based on the method of statistical tests. The depth of an open pit mine is regarded as a random value depending on the errors of the initial data. Distribution of the random depth of open pit mines is investigated and the probable interval of excess of the real value of the depth over the calculated value is determined. Based on the investigations, recommendations are given for the determination of the promising depth and contours of an open pit mine on the surface.

entry.dc:title: DESIGNING THE SACATON CONCENTRATOR.
entry.dc:creator: Mortensen D.K.
entry.dc:description: Asarco's Sacaton unit was brought into ore production in February, 1974, at an estimated capital cost of 40 million. The open pit mine and concentrator, located 45 mi southeast of Phoenix, Ariz. , is expected to recover concentrates containing 21,000 tpy Cu. Ore reserves are currently estimated close to 48 million t at 0. 95% Cu. Sacaton's production schedule calls for the mining of about 41,000 tpd waste and 9000 tpd ore. The Sacaton mineralization contains both sulfide and oxide ores. Primary mineral constituents are chalcocite, azurite, malachite, chrysocolla, and minor amounts of silver and occasional gold. Sulfides are distinguished from oxides when more than half the total copper content is in the form of a sulfide copper mineral. While non-sulfide copper minerals are considerably less prevalent throughout the orebody, they tend to occur quite intimately with the sulfide minerals, particularly in the upper zones of the mineralization. For this reason the decision was made to treat all the ore in a flotation circuit using existing sulfidizing methods. Flowsheet of the concentrator is shown and described.

entry.dc:title: Determination of the Optimal Variant of Development of Mining Work with Blending Operations, Using Mathematical Modeling for Design.
entry.dc:creator: Shugaev I.
entry.dc:description: A method is presented for matehamtical modeling of a deposit and geometric elements of an open pit mine. Calculation of stage-by-stage volumes of mining work and of qualitative indices by means of a computer, and in different variants, is carried out. A mathematical model of the process of ore mining is presented. Based on it, an optimal variant of the development of the mining work with blending operations is selected for project design.

entry.dc:title: HOW TO PLAN OPEN PIT WORKSHOP AND SERVICE FACILITIES.
entry.dc:creator: Rau R.
entry.dc:description: Development of an open pit mine is very expensive; therefore, planning must be thorough. The main criterion is always the highest possible machine availability. In the implementation of the above criterion, paper discusses: planning of workshops and service bays; design of a fuel and lubricants tank farm; wash bays; as well as service of light vehicle and trucks.

entry.dc:title: Methods of Combating Deformations of Clayey Soils at Open Pit Mines in Subcarpathian Area.
entry.dc:creator: Pevzner M.
entry.dc:description: Methods of strengthening of open pit mine edges and slopes of dumps consisting of clayey soils, developed at the yavorov sulfur mining combine, are described. The method consists of the creation of zones of increased hardness with the so-called ″soil piles″ . These are cylindrical soil piles hardened by means of a constant electric field or a composition binder material.

entry.dc:title: Thorium Veins in the United States
entry.dc:creator: Staatz M.
entry.dc:description: 50 Thorium-bearing veins present the largest known potential resource of thorium in the United States in deposits that can be easily exploitable in the near future. Veins of this type are principally of quartz, feldspar, and iron oxides and are known from at least 13 widely scattered areas: extending from Montana to California and New Mexico. Veins in these areas range in length from a few feet to at least 5,000 feet and in thickness from thin seams to 50 feet. Many are 200 to 600 feet long and 0. 5 to 3. 0 feet thick. Thorite is by far the most abundant thorium mineral. Monazite is also commonly present and in a few veins there is brockite and allanite. The thorium content of samples from various veins ranges from 0. 001 to 21. 0 percent ThO//2. The rare-earth content of the veins is substantial and, depending on demand, may be economically as important as the thorium. Although rare earths commonly are present in the same minerals as thorium, there may be little correlation between thorium and rare-earth content in a sample.

entry.dc:title: Experimental with High-Pressure, Down-Hole Rock Drill at the ″Erzberg″ Iron Mine in Austria.
entry.dc:creator: Klobassa O.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: Paper describes the development of the large diameter drilling of blastholes at the iron open pit mine ″Erzberg″ in Austria, with particular emphasis on the introduction of the high-pressure, down-hole percussive drills. The technique is successful wherever the tectonic conditions and hardness of rock do not permit an economical rotary drilling. The anticipated increase of drilling rate and of bit life have been achieved. Investigation of abatement of dust by addition of water to compressed air is being carried on.

entry.dc:title: TRUCK SERVICING AND MAINTENANCE PROGRAM AT KAISER'S EAGLE MOUNTAIN MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Olson E.
entry.dc:description: Open pit mine is located about 80 mi east of Palm Springs, Cal. in an arid area with summer temperatures commonly exceeding 120 F. It produces hematite ore at a rate of between 35 and 60-million tpy with a stripping ratio of 4:1. There are about 75-100 plus capacity haulage trucks for ore and waste employed. Haulage distances vary between 4 and 6 mi for ore and are about 1 mi for waste. Paper describes the truck, service and maintenance program that contributed to a significant increase of : overall truck productivity; average life of diesel engines, transmissions and tires.
